title: Vanuatu Achieves Independence from Anglo-French Condominium
description: Vanuatu gained independence on 30 July 1980 from the unique Anglo-French Condominium that had jointly administered the New Hebrides since 1906, with Father Walter Lini becoming the first Prime Minister. The transition required dismantling parallel British and French legal, education, and administrative systems.

title: Espiritu Santo Coconut War Secession Attempt
description: Jimmy Stevens led the Nagriamel movement in declaring the independent state of Vemerana on Espiritu Santo island in May 1980, threatening Vanuatu's territorial integrity at independence. The secession was suppressed by Papua New Guinea Defence Force troops with logistical Australian support, ending the so-called Coconut War by August.

title: Vanuatu Joins United Nations and Commonwealth
description: Vanuatu was admitted to the United Nations on 15 September 1981 and the Commonwealth of Nations the same year. The young state quickly emerged as one of the most diplomatically active Pacific microstates, joining the Non-Aligned Movement.

title: Vanuatu Joins Non-Aligned Movement
description: Father Walter Lini's government formally aligned Vanuatu with the Non-Aligned Movement in 1983, an unusual stance for a small Pacific state. The decision reflected Lini's Melanesian-socialist worldview and produced ties with Cuba, Libya, and the Soviet Union that alarmed Western partners.

title: Father Walter Lini Ousted from Power
description: Father Walter Lini was forced out of the Vanua'aku Pati leadership and the prime ministership in August 1991 after years of internal disputes, ending an 11-year tenure as the founding leader of independent Vanuatu. His ousting opened a long era of unstable coalition politics.

title: Mobile Defence Force Mutiny in Port Vila
description: Members of the Vanuatu Mobile Force briefly seized President Jean-Marie Leye in October 1996 in a pay dispute that escalated into a mutiny. The crisis was resolved through negotiation but exposed the fragility of civilian control over uniformed services.

title: Vanuatu National Provident Fund Riots
description: Riots broke out in Port Vila in January 1998 after restrictions were placed on withdrawals from the Vanuatu National Provident Fund, causing extensive property damage and a state of emergency. The unrest produced an inquiry that found systematic mismanagement of the pension scheme.

title: Comprehensive Reform Programme Launched
description: Vanuatu launched a Comprehensive Reform Programme with Asian Development Bank backing, restructuring the public service, financial sector, and tax system. The reforms were politically contentious and only partially implemented before successive governments diluted them.

title: Tannese-Ambrymese Tensions Force State of Emergency
description: Communal violence between Tannese and Ambrymese settlers in the Blacksands area of Port Vila in March 2007 left at least three dead and forced a state of emergency. The unrest revealed the strains of urban migration on inter-island social cohesion.

title: Vanuatu and Solomon Islands Sign Border Treaty
description: Vanuatu and Solomon Islands signed a maritime boundary treaty in 2014 resolving long-standing border questions in the Coral Sea and Reef Islands area. The agreement provided certainty for fisheries management and resource development.

title: Cyclone Pam Devastates Vanuatu
description: Severe Tropical Cyclone Pam struck Vanuatu on 13 March 2015 as a Category 5 storm, killing 11 people directly and devastating roughly 90 percent of buildings on Efate and southern islands. Damages were estimated at USD 449 million, equivalent to over 60 percent of GDP, in the worst disaster in the country's history.

title: Fourteen MPs Convicted of Corruption in Mass Trial
description: Vanuatu's Supreme Court convicted 14 of 52 sitting MPs of corruption and bribery offences in October 2015, including Deputy Prime Minister Moana Carcasses Kalosil. The convictions, in a single mass trial, removed more than a quarter of parliament and represented one of the largest political-corruption prosecutions ever in the Pacific.

title: Speaker Issues Self-Pardon to Reverse Convictions
description: Acting President Marcellino Pipite, while serving as Speaker, attempted to pardon himself and his fellow convicted MPs days after the corruption convictions. The pardons were quickly revoked when President Lonsdale returned from overseas, in an episode that captured global attention.

title: Snap Election Replaces Convicted Parliament
description: Following the corruption convictions and speaker self-pardon scandal, Vanuatu held a snap election in January 2016 that returned Charlot Salwai as Prime Minister leading a new coalition. The vote was widely seen as restoring democratic legitimacy.

title: Manaro Volcano Forces Mass Evacuation of Ambae
description: Increased activity at the Manaro Voui volcano on Ambae prompted the evacuation of all 11,000 residents in September 2017 and again in 2018. The displacement, eventually permanent for many, was one of the largest volcanic evacuations in the Pacific in decades.

title: Vanuatu and Cuba Establish Diplomatic Relations
description: Vanuatu and Cuba established formal diplomatic relations in 2018, building on long-standing health and education cooperation. The decision reflected Vanuatu's tradition of independent foreign policy outside the dominant Western framework.

title: Vanuatu Adopts Strictest Plastics Ban in the Pacific
description: Vanuatu introduced one of the world's strictest single-use plastics bans on 1 July 2018, prohibiting plastic bags, straws, and polystyrene takeaway boxes. The policy positioned the country as a global leader on ocean plastics regulation.

title: Cyclone Harold Strikes Vanuatu During COVID-19 Lockdown
description: Severe Tropical Cyclone Harold struck Vanuatu on 6 April 2020 as a Category 5 storm, devastating Espiritu Santo and Pentecost while the country was in COVID-19 lockdown. Damages reached around USD 600 million, about 60 percent of GDP, and complicated the pandemic emergency response.

title: Vanuatu Graduates from Least Developed Country Status
description: Vanuatu graduated from the United Nations Least Developed Country category on 4 December 2020 after years of postponements due to disasters. Graduation was a milestone of development progress but also ended preferential trade access.

title: Vanuatu and Russia Establish Diplomatic Relations
description: Vanuatu and Russia formalised diplomatic relations in 2022 amid the Ukraine war and intensifying global geopolitical competition. The move was criticised by Western partners but defended in Port Vila as consistent with Vanuatu's non-aligned tradition.

title: Vanuatu Leads UN General Assembly ICJ Climate Resolution
description: Vanuatu spearheaded a coalition of states in 2022-2023 that secured a UN General Assembly resolution requesting an International Court of Justice advisory opinion on the legal obligations of states regarding climate change. The diplomatic campaign, originated by Pacific law students, became one of Vanuatu's most internationally visible initiatives.

title: Twin Category 4 Cyclones Strike Within 72 Hours
description: Vanuatu was struck by Tropical Cyclones Judy and Kevin within 72 hours in March 2023, both reaching Category 4 strength and causing widespread destruction across multiple provinces. The unprecedented twin landfalls were cited internationally as evidence of compounding climate-driven disaster risk.

title: ICJ Advisory Opinion on Climate Change Adopted by UNGA
description: The UN General Assembly formally adopted Vanuatu's resolution requesting an ICJ advisory opinion on climate change obligations on 29 March 2023 by consensus. The opinion process opened a new front in international climate jurisprudence.

title: Vanuatu Cycles Through Three Prime Ministers in One Year
description: Vanuatu cycled through Prime Ministers Ishmael Kalsakau, Sato Kilman, and then Charlot Salwai across 2023, exemplifying the chronic instability of Vanuatu's coalition politics. The churn raised renewed calls for constitutional and electoral reform.

title: Magnitude 7.3 Earthquake Strikes Port Vila
description: A magnitude 7.3 earthquake struck off Efate on 17 December 2024, killing at least 14 people and damaging significant parts of central Port Vila including embassies, hospitals, and the main wharf. The disaster temporarily disrupted government operations and required international urban search and rescue support.

title: Constitutional Referendum Tightens Anti-Defection Rules
description: Vanuatu held a constitutional referendum in May 2024 that overwhelmingly approved amendments tightening anti-defection rules to curb the rampant party-hopping that fuels government instability. The reforms aim to make it materially costlier for MPs to switch parties mid-term.

title: Charlot Salwai Returns as Prime Minister
description: Following the January 2025 general election triggered by post-earthquake political pressures, Charlot Salwai returned to office as Prime Minister leading a new coalition. Salwai pledged a focus on earthquake recovery and implementing the constitutional anti-defection reforms.

title: ICJ Issues Landmark Climate Advisory Opinion
description: The International Court of Justice issued its advisory opinion in 2025 on the obligations of states in respect of climate change, the culmination of Vanuatu's multi-year diplomatic campaign. The opinion was widely cited as a foundational moment for climate-change international law.

title: Yasur Volcano Activity Disrupts Tanna Tourism
description: Continuing elevated activity at Mount Yasur on Tanna island in 2025 prompted access restrictions and intermittent disruption of the country's most prominent tourism attraction. The episode underlined the ongoing role of active volcanism in Vanuatu's economy and risk landscape.
